title: Membership in the Church
definition: Membership in the Church is the committed belonging of believers to a local body for worship, care, accountability, and mission.
summary: Membership in the Church is a believer's committed identification with a local congregation for care, accountability, service, and mission.
christFocus: Jesus Christ gathers His sheep into accountable communities under His shepherding care.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: This doctrine focuses on recognized commitment. Membership says, 'These are my people, these are my shepherds, and this is where I will be known and serve.' It gives practical shape to responsibilities that cannot be fulfilled in vague attachment.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This matters because casual attendance can avoid both accountability and responsibility. Membership helps pastors know whom they shepherd and helps believers know whom they are called to love and serve. It also protects the church's witness by clarifying who represents the congregation.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Treat membership as covenantal commitment, not consumer enrollment. Be willing to be known, corrected, encouraged, and needed. Help your church make membership meaningful rather than merely administrative.
